This image shows a Turkish cannonball embedded in the wall of St. Stephen's Cathedral in Vienna, commemorating the 1683 Ottoman siege.
Historical Relic: Known locally as a Türkenkugel (Turkish ball), it is one of several such projectiles still visible in the city center from the sieges of 1529 and 1683.
Specific Location: The cannonball is embedded in the stone facade of St. Stephen's Cathedral, which was a central point during the battle.
Commemorative Detail: The year "1683" is painted in white below the cannonball to mark the date of the second Turkish siege.
Symbolism: These cannonballs serve as lasting scars of history, reminding residents and visitors of Vienna's defense against Ottoman expansion.
